blocks.prompt: 3 In how many ways can five subjects be selected out of eight subjects to select a course programme?
blocks.explanation:
A course programme is a set of subjects; the order of picking them does not matter.
We must count the selections of 5 subjects from 8.
Plan: this is a combination, \({}^{8}C_{5}\).
steps:
Given: 8 subjects; 5 are to be selected.
To find: the number of different course programmes.
Method: Order does not matter (Physics, Chemistry, ... is the same course as Chemistry, Physics, ...), so use \({}^{n}C_{r}\) with \(n = 8\), \(r = 5\).

Check
\[{}^{8}C_{5} = {}^{8}C_{3} = \dfrac{8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6}{6} = 56\]
Why: Choosing 5 subjects to take is the same as choosing 3 to leave out.
